attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Here' is fairly read as the AI compute chain he describes. It is a present-tense factual claim. His aside names resellers (Dell, Supermicro) without saying they are unprofitable, which leaves the boundary of the chain ambiguous.

contract.note: The plain reading (profit from the AI-chain activity after attributable costs) is ordinary given his talk of debt and losses. It fairly excludes profits from unrelated businesses. The result still depends on which profit measure is used and on where the chain's boundary is drawn.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's primary filing shows positive GAAP net income for the quarter ended Oct 26, 2025. This fits the NVIDIA half of the claim but says nothing about whether NVIDIA is the only profitable participant.
CoreWeave reported a net loss for Q3 2025 even with positive adjusted operating income. This fits his description of one participant but cannot show that every other participant lacked profit.
AWS segment operating income is positive, but the segment mixes AI and non-AI services. The contract excludes broad cloud profit as proof.

Secondary report on private Oracle documents: a 14% gross margin on NVIDIA server rentals, which would still be about 7% after the extra depreciation. That suggests positive margin, but it leaves out financing and other costs, and the underlying records were unseen.

reviews.rationale: NVIDIA's profit is established. The packet has no comparable profit figures for AI activity after all attributable costs across the other participants. CoreWeave's loss fits the claim. The AWS and Oracle figures suggest positive margins, but only on bases the contract says cannot settle the question. Resellers named in the aside are not examined. The evidence neither confirms nor refutes the claim that only NVIDIA profits.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter. The $1.21T figure comes from his own estimate.

semantics.note: Reading 'profit' as AI profit fits the context ('this capex is only for AI'). The draft leaves out the ~$605B capex basis and the 'at the time I calculated it' qualifier, and it rests on his own 2:1 multiplier. The contract restores both points.

contract.note: Scoring 'profit' as AI-attributable profit, not consolidated profit, is a fair ordinary reading. The contract rightly leaves open whether 'hole' means a gross requirement or a remaining shortfall. The 2:1 multiplier is the speaker's own modelling assumption and is hard to verify independently.

evidence.note: Microsoft's quarterly capex of $34.9B covers cloud and AI together. It does not establish cumulative AI capex or AI profit.
Alphabet's consolidated operating results are positive, but they include non-AI businesses. They neither contradict nor confirm the claim about AI profit.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no AI-specific profit-and-loss figures for the four companies. It also has no reconciliation of the ~$605B cumulative capex and no check of the 2:1 revenue requirement. Consolidated results and quarterly capex are context only, and missing AI disclosures are not proof of zero profit. The evidence does not settle the claim.
